---
title: "🚀 Quick Start"
---

## 📦 Install

To install searcherkit, directly clone the repository and install:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ml-stat-Sustech/searcherkit.git
cd searcherkit
pip install -e .
```

## 🧩 Additional Dependencies

### 📁 Search local files

The built-in `file` source uses `rg` for full-text search. Install
[ripgrep](https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep) and make sure `rg` is on
`PATH` before using file-backed search tools.

### 🗄️ Search knowledge bases

SearcherKit supports knowledge bases hosted on Elasticsearch. The Elasticsearch
client is included in the default installation. You need an active Elasticsearch
(`version < 9.0.0`) instance to use the `elasticsearch` source. To deploy a local
Elasticsearch knowledge base, see [Build Elasticsearch knowledge base](04-advanced-usage/03-source-advanced-usage.qmd).

### 🧠 Search with embeddings

SearcherKit supports embedding-based search for elasticsearch source. To deploy a local embedding model, see [Serve embedding model](./02-basics/02-source.qmd).

## 🖥️ Begin search

SearcherKit provides a command-line interface `searcherkit ...` to use the package.
The TUI and its dependencies are included in the default installation.

First, prepare a config file specifying the model, tools and search sources.

### 🤖 Configure LLM Endpoints

Configure the LLM model name, endpoint URL, and API key under the
`agent.llm_client` section. The Anthropic client is included in the default
installation; specify `type: anthropic` to connect to an Anthropic-compatible
endpoint.

```{.yaml filename="config.yaml"}
agent:
  llm_client:
    type: openai # openai or anthropic
    model: MODEL_NAME # specify the model name, e.g. "qwen3-8b"
    api_key: API_KEY # specify the API key
    base_url: BASE_URL # specify the base URL
```

### 🔎 Configure search sources

Configure the search sources to specify where you want to search from.

```{.yaml filename="config.py"}
agent:
  sources:
    - type: file
      name: file_source
      root_path: /path/to/search/from  # specify the root path for file search

    - type: elasticsearch
      name: elasticsearch_source
      hosts: ["http://127.0.0.1:9200"]
      index: elasticsearch_index
      es_max_concurrency: 1024

    - type: web
      name: web_source
      serper_api_key: API_KEY
      jina_api_key: API_KEY
```

For advanced configuration, see [Source and Tool](02-basics/02-source.qmd)

### 🛠️ Configure tools

`SearcherKit` provides two tools out-of-the-box.

`search` tool takes search query(s) and an optional `top_k`. It returns a list of documents related to the query(s) with the length of `top_k`

`visit` tool takes document_id(s) and an optional `goal` string. It returns the full text of the document(s) with provided id(s). If `summarizer` is provided, it returns a summary of the document about the topic provided in `goal`. (See [Summerizer](./02-basics/03-tool.qmd))

To use the tools, specify which source the tools will search & visit from

Use `type: custom` and specify `target` for custom tools. On making new custom tools see [Custom Tools](04-advanced-usage/01-custom-modules.qmd)

```{.yaml filename="config.yaml"}
agent:
  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search
      source:
        - file_1

    - type: visit
      name: visit
      source:
        - file_1

    - type: custom
      target: pkg://import.string.to::ToolClass # or file://file.path.to::ToolClass
      extra:
        param1: value1
```


### ▶️ Start the agent

Save the configuration file to any directory. E.g. `/path/to/config/config_name.yaml`. Here's an example of a full config.

```{.yaml filename="/path/to/config/config_name.yaml"}
agent:
  sources:
    - type: file
      name: file_source
      root_path: /path/to/search/from

  tools:
    - type: search
      name: search
      source:
        - file_1

    - type: visit
      name: visit
      source:
        - file_1

  # specify system prompt for the agent
  system_prompt: "Use the available search and visit tools when they can verify the answer. Put the final answer in <answer></answer> tags."

  llm_retry_config:
    exceptions:
      - pkg://searcherkit.llm.parsers:ParsingError

output_path: outputs/agent_history

logging:
  global_file: ${output_path}/run.log
  trace:
    enabled: true
    dir: ${output_path}/traces
    format: text
    level: DEBUG
    filename_template: "{sample_id}_{trace_id}.log"
```

- See [config.yaml](../../src/searcherkit/config/config.yaml) for full configuration.
- See [searcherkit.yaml](../../src/searcherkit/config/searcherkit.yaml) for a more detailed configuration for `elasticsearch` source.

Use the `inspect` command to check if the config is legal

```bash
searcherkit inspect --config-path /path/to/config --config-name config_name
```

If the config is correct, the following message would be shown:

```
Config validation passed. No issues found.
```

Finally, to run the agent. start searcherkit TUI with the command:

```bash
searcherkit tui --config-path /path/to/config --config-name config_name
```

To run agent tasks in batch, specify input dataset with `dataloader.source` and output directory with `output_path`, then run with `run` command:

```bash
searcherkit run \
  --config-path /path/to/config \
  --config-name config_name \
  +dataloader.source /path/to/dataset.jsonl \
  +output_path /output/directory
```

See [Run and Evaluate](./02-basics/05-run-and-evaluation.qmd) for details

Finally, to evaluate the run result, use the `evaluate` command
```bash
export OPENAI_BASE_URL="https://127.0.0.1/v1"
export OPENAI_API_KEY=""

searcherkit evaluate \
    /path/to/input \
    /path/to/output \
    --max-concurrency 128 \
    --answer-pattern '\\boxed\{(?P<answer>[^}]*)\}'
```

See [evaluate](02-basics/05-run-and-evaluation.qmd) for details

## Examples

Start from `src/searcherkit/config/config.yaml` or one of the packaged model configs:

| Config | Parser | Tool interface |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `webexplorer.yaml` | `upstream` | Batched `search(queries)` and `browse(url, query)` |
| `websailor.yaml` | `websailor` | Batched `search(query)` and `visit(url, goal)` |
| `tongyi_deepresearch.yaml` | `tongyi_deep_research` | Batched `search(query)` and `visit(url, goal)` |

These files contain deployment-specific model paths, endpoints, index names, and high concurrency defaults. Copy one and replace those values for your environment or use hydra-style command-line overrides. The essential fields are the client, parser, sources, tools, data, and output directory.

### Embedding Model

For deploying a local embedding model, we recommend using [Text Embeddings Inference](https://github.com/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference), A blazing fast inference solution for text embeddings models.

### LLM Model

We recommend using [vLLM](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) or [SGLang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang) to deploy your model.

For better KV Cache hit rate, we recommand replace data parallel config with dedicated server setup.

For example, for a `dp=2, tp=2` setup, start 2 seperate servers with `dp=1, tp=2`.

Pass the corresponding endpoint URLs in a list to the agent config:

```yaml
agent:
  llm_client:
    base_url:
      - http://127.0.0.1:8001
      - http://127.0.0.1:8002
```

The agent runner will bind each session to a single endpoint to maximize cache hits.

### Deploy embedding database as search source

```bash
  --es_host http://127.0.0.1:9200 \
  --index_name browsecomp_plus_qwen3 \
  --dense-vector \
  --model_name /models/Qwen3-Embedding-8B \
  --embedding_dim 4096 \
  --prompt_strategy qwen3 \
  --overwrite
```
